title: Cycle orchestration: Scope Fishing Lanes and adaptive capacity allocation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose:
This playbook defines a structured approach to cycle planning that reserves explicit lightweight 'fishing lanes' — small, time-boxed capacity bands for high-impact emergent work — while preserving committed scope for OKRs and cross-team initiatives. The goal is to reduce mid-cycle chaos, make scope cuts predictable, and improve confidence in hitting OKR commitments.

Background / Problem statement:
- In past cycles we either over-committed and missed OKRs, or we under-allocated and wasted engineering momentum.
- Unplanned customer escalations and legal/regulatory requests frequently arrive mid-cycle and currently disrupt the committed plan.
- Existing tranche and buffer playbooks are broad; teams ask for a lightweight operational protocol that is easy to apply at the team and initiative level.

Proposal (high-level):
1) Define three capacity lanes per cycle at the initiative level: Committed (70%), Flexible (20%), Fishing (10%). Percentages are configurable by project risk profile.
2) Committed lane: items scoped, estimated, and owned by initiative leads. Changes require formal scope-change approval.
3) Flexible lane: planned low-risk stretch items prioritized in backlog; can be promoted into Committed with PM + Eng tech lead signoff.
4) Fishing lane: reserved tickets for high-impact emergent work (customer bugs, legal/security asks, urgent infra fixes). Activation requires on-call PM + Eng approval and a triage ticket with owner and target impact metric.
5) Weekly capacity burn reviews: initiative leads report lane utilization and reallocate within a predefined guardrail matrix.

Scope-cut rules and triggers:
- Soft trigger: when Committed+Flexible burn > 85% of forecast before cycle midpoint -> initiate scope freeze review.
- Hard trigger: when Committed burn > 95% or unexpected Fishing activation > 2x allocated slots -> automatic reprioritization meeting within 48 hours.
- Cut order: non-customer-facing stretch features -> docs/localization -> deferred infra improvements -> last resort: trimmed slices of committed features with rollback plan.

Acceptance criteria:
- Playbook adopted by at least 3 cross-functional initiatives in the next cycle pilot.
- Clear checklist for Fishing lane activation in the console (triage ticket created, owner assigned, impact metric declared).
- Cycle-level dashboard visible to leads showing lane allocations and live utilization.

Rollout plan:
- Week 0: socialize playbook in PM sync and engineering all-hands; update initiative templates.
- Week 1: pilot with two initiatives (one Platform, one Hosting) and provide a short one-pager for squads.
- Mid-cycle: gather feedback and adjust default lane splits.
- Post-cycle: run a blameless retrospective and measure OKR completion delta vs prior cycles.

Notes on sizing and fairness:
- Default 70/20/10 is a starting point — high-risk initiatives (e.g., new infra) may set 60/25/15.
- Leads must document expected candidate items for Fishing lane at beginning of cycle (even if empty) to reduce ad-hoc backlog creation.

Operational integrations:
- Console: add an Initiative view with lane columns and a simple toggle to 'activate fishing slot' that creates a prefilled Linear ticket template.
- Alerts: add a threshold alert to the initiative dashboard for the soft/hard triggers.
- Templates: Confluence PRD template updated with lane allocation fields and decision owner names.

Implementation risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Teams misuse Fishing lane as extra runway for low-priority work -> mitigation: require documented customer/regulatory justification and PM+Eng approval.
- Risk: Overhead of weekly reporting -> mitigation: automate utilization reporting from Linear/Console and provide lightweight default reports.

Ownership and next steps:
- PM owner: Aisha Patel (playbook shepherd).
- Engineering partner: Marcus Nguyen (implementation/console wiring).
- Design: inform UI for 'activate fishing slot' flow (DES-204).
- Next steps: finalize playbook, create console ticket templates, schedule pilot kickoff for 2026-W11.
